rules.reason: denominations are reference data, not private records: any signed-in user needs to know that BTC divides into eight places in order to render an amount correctly at all
operators may add their own units (a gift-card program, a loyalty point, a barter unit) but cannot edit the seeded ones everybody shares

public pages that display money (an invoice pay link, a storefront) must be able to resolve the scale of a standard unit; operator-defined denominations stay behind the sign-in because a custom code can name a business relationship

rates are shared observations: any signed-in user may read them (an amount cannot be valued without one) and may record one they fetched. No update or delete -- a restated rate is a new row with a later fetched_at, never an edit to what was recorded at the time
signed-in users manage the chart of accounts they created
signed-in users manage journals they created, including the draft->posted transition guarded on the schema
signed-in users manage line items on journals they created
signed-in users manage recurring journal templates they created
the accounts page is public; it shows a sign-in prompt to visitors
the journals page is public; it shows a sign-in prompt to visitors
the trial balance page is public; it shows a sign-in prompt to visitors and the page itself scopes the report to the signed-in owner (see objects/site/trial_balance.py)
setup-accounts is public execute like every other finance page object; the object itself requires a signed-in identity and verifies the entity belongs to the caller before creating any account
reversing a posted journal is the doctrine-correct correction; the object itself enforces owner-or-admin on the target journal
